name: Learn basic punching combinations
blurb: Four punches — jab, cross, hook, uppercut — and the handful of combinations built from them. Power comes from the ground up through rotation, never from the arm.
gear: Hand wraps and bag gloves if you use a bag
A heavy bag or just a mirror
steps: Learn the jab: lead hand straight out and back fast, rear hand glued to the chin, shoulder shielding the jaw.
Learn the cross: rear-foot pivot, hip rotation, then the arm. The punch is the last thing to happen.
Learn the lead hook with the elbow at shoulder height and the whole body turning as one unit.
Learn the uppercut, driven by a small dip and leg drive rather than a scooping arm.
Drill the standard combinations: 1-2, 1-2-3, 1-1-2, 2-3-2, always returning hands to guard.
Add movement so every combination starts and finishes with footwork.
tips: Dropping the non-punching hand is the universal beginner habit and the one that gets you hit.
Never punch a bag bare-knuckled or with locked elbows. Wraps first, always.
Snap the punch back. Leaving it out there is slower and less powerful.
proof: Three rounds on the bag with correct rotation, tight guard and clean combinations.
